To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Herschel SPIRIT FTS spectra show the CO ladder in M82 up to high rotational levels.
we have observed CO lines in M82 up to J=13-12 for the first time with SPIRE FTS.

Herschel-Spire observations of the CO ladder of M82 show a warm molecular gas component (similar to 500 K) that is likely heated by dissipation in the ISM rather than by X-rays and UV radiation from the straburb.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the molecular interstellar matter in the central region of the starbursting galaxy M82.
the study of the interstellar medium of the starburst M82 galaxy, with particular emphasis on the physical conditions of the molecular gas.
understanding the physical conditions and dynamics of the ISM in galaxies and their evolution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Herschel observations of M82 are a triumph of the FTS and a major step forward in understanding the molecular interstellar matter.
the warm molecular gas is heated by turbulence dissipation in M82.
the molecular gas of M82 is warm, dense, and turbulent, and that this warm and dense gas is heated by the dissipation of turbulence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SPIRE FTA is an ideal instrument for the study of molecular lines from galaxies, and that the SPIRE spectrometer is an ideal tool for the study of warm molecular gas.
we have been able to probe the molecular ISM of M82 with a single spectrum, and have been able to constrain the physical properties of the molecular gas in the central region of the galaxy.
Herschel has provided the best view yet of the warm molecular gas in M82.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SPIRE Focal Plane Array (FPA) has a large dynamic range, which allows the study of faint lines in the presence of a strong continuum.
the warm molecular gas is a major component of the ISM in the central region of starburst galaxies.
the high-J CO lines are very sensitive to the physical conditions of the gas and are therefore a good probe of the warm and dense gas in the ISM.
